# Copilot Instructions for kasm-registry

## What This Repository Does

This is a **custom Kasm Workspaces registry** (forked/based on the official template). It provides:
- A **static Next.js website** that lists available Docker-based workspaces for [Kasm Workspaces](https://kasmweb.com/).
- A **JSON processing pipeline** that converts per-workspace JSON config files into a single `list.json` registry API file consumed by Kasm Workspaces.
- **Multi-schema-version support** via git branches (e.g., branch `1.0` for schema v1.0, branch `1.1` for schema v1.1). The CI build compiles all branches and deploys them together to GitHub Pages.

The live site is hosted on GitHub Pages and deployed automatically on every push via GitHub Actions.

---

## Repository Structure

```
kasm-registry/
├── .github/
│   └── workflows/
│       └── build-and-deploy.yml   # CI: builds all branches → deploys to gh-pages
├── processing/                    # Node.js scripts that generate registry metadata
│   ├── processjson.js             # Main script: reads workspaces/ → writes public/list.json at repo root
│   ├── add_next_version.js        # Bulk-adds a new Kasm version to every workspace
│   ├── get_image_sizes.js         # Pulls Docker images to measure uncompressed sizes
│   ├── update_1_0_to_1_1.js       # One-time migration from schema 1.0 → 1.1
│   └── package.json
├── site/                          # Next.js static frontend
│   ├── pages/
│   │   ├── index.js               # Home page: workspace browser with search & version filter
│   │   ├── _app.js                # App wrapper: global search state
│   │   └── new/[[...workspace]].js # Workspace builder/editor page
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── Workspace.js           # Workspace card component
│   │   ├── header.js              # Navigation and search bar
│   │   ├── layout.js              # Page layout wrapper
│   │   ├── footer.js              # Footer component
│   │   └── Bubbles.js             # Background decoration
│   ├── styles/
│   ├── public/
│   │   ├── list.json              # Committed seed file (provides initial data for the dev server); overwrite by copying from repo-root public/ after running processjson.js
│   │   └── favicon.ico
│   ├── next.config.js             # Registry name, description, icon, URLs, basePath
│   ├── tailwind.config.js
│   └── package.json
├── workspaces/                    # One folder per workspace with workspace.json + icon image
│   └── UbuntuDesktopTor/
│       ├── workspace.json
│       └── ubuntu.png
├── public/                        # Generated output (DO NOT edit by hand; created at build time)
│   ├── list.json                  # Generated by processjson.js
│   ├── versions.json              # Generated by processjson.js
│   └── icons/                    # Workspace icons (copied from workspaces/ by processjson.js)
├── build_all_branches.sh          # Builds every git branch and assembles the output in /public
└── README.md
```

## Key Configuration: `site/next.config.js`

This file controls registry metadata shown to users. Edit the `env` block to customise the registry:

```js
env: {
  name: 'My Registry Name',
  description: 'Short description shown in Kasm Workspaces UI.',
  icon: 'https://example.com/icon.png',
  listUrl: 'https://username.github.io/kasm-registry/',   // trailing slash required
  contactUrl: 'https://github.com/username/kasm-registry/issues',
},
basePath: '/kasm-registry/1.0',   // NOTE: "1.0" is replaced with the branch name during build
```

**Important:** The `basePath` always uses `1.0` as a placeholder; `build_all_branches.sh` uses `sed` to substitute the actual branch name at build time. Never hard-code the real branch name here.

## How to Build & Run Locally

### Prerequisites
- Node.js (LTS recommended)
- npm

### Development workflow

```bash
# 1. Install dependencies
npm ci --prefix processing
npm ci --prefix site

# 2. Generate public/list.json and public/icons/ from workspaces (must run before starting the site)
node processing                              # writes to ./public/ at repo root
cp public/list.json site/public/list.json    # make the dev server pick up the updated registry
cp -r public/icons site/public/              # make icons available to the dev server
# Re-run these two cp lines whenever you add or modify workspaces during development

# 3. Start the Next.js dev server
npm run dev --prefix site        # http://localhost:3000
```

### Production build (mirrors CI)

```bash
npm ci --prefix processing
npm ci --prefix site
./build_all_branches.sh          # Builds all branches; output goes to /public
```

### Lint

```bash
npm run lint --prefix site       # ESLint (Next.js rules)
```

### Tests

There is **no automated test suite** in this repository. Build success and lint passing are the only automated quality gates.

## Adding or Editing a Workspace

1. Create a new folder inside `workspaces/` (e.g., `workspaces/MyNewWorkspace/`).
2. Add a `workspace.json` file (schema 1.1 – see below).
3. Add an icon image (`.png` or `.svg`, square, ≥ 50 × 50 px). The filename must match the `image_src` field.
4. Commit and push – the CI pipeline will regenerate `list.json` and redeploy the site.

### workspace.json schema (v1.1)

```json
{
  "friendly_name": "My Workspace",
  "description": "Short description of the workspace.",
  "image_src": "my-workspace.png",
  "docker_registry": "https://index.docker.io/v1/",
  "architecture": ["amd64", "arm64"],
  "categories": ["Development"],
  "compatibility": [
    {
      "version": "1.16.x",
      "image": "myrepo/myimage:1.16",
      "uncompressed_size_mb": 2500,
      "available_tags": ["develop", "1.16.0"]
    }
  ],
  "run_config": {},
  "exec_config": {},
  "cores": 2,
  "memory": 2768,
  "gpu_count": 0,
  "cpu_allocation_method": "Inherit"
}
```

**Field notes:**
- `friendly_name`, `description`, `image_src`, `architecture`, `compatibility` are **required**.
- `categories` should contain at most 3 values.
- `uncompressed_size_mb` is the approximate uncompressed Docker image size in MB.
- `available_tags` defines **channels** (e.g., `develop`, `1.16.0`). Omit this key entirely if you do not want channel support. If you use `available_tags` on any workspace, add it to all workspaces for consistency.
- `cpu_allocation_method` must be `"Inherit"`, `"Quotas"`, or `"Shares"`.

## CI/CD Pipeline

**File:** `.github/workflows/build-and-deploy.yml`

**Trigger:** Every `push` to any branch except `gh-pages`.

**Steps:**
1. `npm ci --prefix processing` – install processing dependencies.
2. `npm ci --prefix site` – install site dependencies.
3. `./build_all_branches.sh` – loops through all remote branches (excluding `HEAD`, `develop`, `gh-pages`), checks out each one, runs `node processing` (which runs `processjson.js`), builds the Next.js site with an adjusted `basePath`, and assembles output in `/public`.
4. Deploys the `/public` directory to the `gh-pages` branch using `JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4`.

**Required repository permission:** `contents: write` (already set in the workflow).

---

## Multi-Branch / Multi-Version Architecture

- Each git branch represents a schema version (e.g., `1.0`, `1.1`).
- Each branch's built site is published under a `/<branchname>/` subdirectory on GitHub Pages (e.g., `/1.0/`, `/1.1/`).
- The GitHub Pages root (`/`) contains a lightweight `index.html` that **meta-refresh redirects** to the default branch subdirectory (the latest schema version).
- `build_all_branches.sh` automates building all branches in a single CI run and assembles the `/public` output with the redirect root and per-branch subdirectories.
- When creating a new schema branch, name it after the schema version (e.g., `1.2`), set it as the default branch, and push – the CI will pick it up automatically.

---

## Processing Scripts (`processing/`)

Run all scripts from the **repo root** after installing dependencies with `npm ci --prefix processing`:

| Script | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `node processing` (run from repo root) | Read all `workspaces/**/workspace.json` files, generate `public/list.json` and `public/versions.json` at the repo root, copy icons to `public/icons/`. **Run this before building or starting the dev server.** |
| `node processing/add_next_version.js` | Bulk-add a new Kasm version entry to every workspace (edit `baseversion` in the script first). Sets `uncompressed_size_mb: 0` so `get_image_sizes.js` can fill it in. |
| `node processing/get_image_sizes.js` | Pull each Docker image with `uncompressed_size_mb: 0`, measure size, update `workspace.json`. Can be restarted if interrupted. |
| `node processing/update_1_0_to_1_1.js` | One-time migration: converts schema 1.0 workspaces to schema 1.1 format. |

## Common Errors & Workarounds

### CI: Only the latest schema branch builds (older branches missing)
Symptom: `1.1` builds correctly but `1.0` output is missing.  
Cause: `git fetch --all` missing from `build_all_branches.sh`.  
Fix: Open `build_all_branches.sh`, find the `echo "All branches:"` line, and ensure `git fetch --all` appears on the next line (already present in this repo).

### `node processing` fails with "Cannot find module"
Cause: `npm ci --prefix processing` was not run first.  
Fix: Run `npm ci --prefix processing` before running any script in `processing/`.

### Site shows no workspaces / `list.json` is empty or stale
Cause: `processjson.js` was not run before building the site.  
Fix: Run `node processing` from the repo root first, then copy `public/list.json` to `site/public/list.json` for the dev server, then build.

### Icon not appearing for a workspace
Cause: The `image_src` filename in `workspace.json` does not match the actual image file in the workspace folder.  
Fix: Ensure the filenames match exactly (case-sensitive on Linux). When the icon file is absent, `processjson.js` logs an error message (currently appearing as something like `undefined/<file>` due to a minor bug in its missing-file check).

### `basePath` issues (404 on sub-pages or wrong URLs)
Cause: `basePath` in `site/next.config.js` set to the wrong value, or missing `trailingSlash: true`.  
Fix: Keep `basePath` with `1.0` as the version placeholder (not the actual branch name). The build script replaces it automatically.

### GitHub Pages not updating after a push
Cause: The Actions workflow may need to be enabled for the first time after forking.  
Fix: Go to **Actions** tab, enable workflows if prompted, then re-trigger by pushing a commit.

---

## Tips for Working Efficiently

- **Never edit `public/list.json`, `public/versions.json`, or `public/icons/` by hand.** These are generated artifacts – always edit the source `workspaces/` files and re-run `node processing`.
- The `site/next.config.js` `env` variables are baked into the static site at build time and exposed to frontend components via `process.env.name`, `process.env.icon`, etc.
- The workspace builder page (`/new/`) lets users create or edit workspace JSON configs in-browser. It pre-generates a static page per workspace via `getStaticPaths`.
- Channel/tag filtering is client-side only; the registry API (`list.json`) includes all workspaces and tags.
- Version preference is stored in `localStorage` on the client.
- Icons should be **square** and at least **50 × 50 px**. Both `.png` and `.svg` are supported.
- When adding a large number of workspaces at once, run `node add_next_version.js` → `node get_image_sizes.js` to automate filling in `uncompressed_size_mb` values.
